- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is falling.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak or use 3-period moving average.  
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 2+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.0x the deviation from prior period’s true value.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is neutral or declining, model often lags; add 0.5–1.0x the recent 7-day average deviation to forecast.  
- If true outcome is consistently below model (e.g., 3+ days), check sentiment for “bearish” signals; if present, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day.  
- If sentiment is “bullish” but model is flat or falling, model may be underreacting; increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
